chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu al-Hasan al-Shami, from Burayd, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), in the case of

a man who accuses all the people with a single word, he said to him: If he does not name them specifically, then only one hadd (fixed punishment) is upon him; and if he names them, then upon him is a hadd for each man.

key_terms.يَقْذِفُ: to accuse (specifically of zina or general misconduct)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for accusing a group of people with one statement in Shia hadith statement?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Istibsar clarifies the distinction between general defamation (qadhf) and specific accusations, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that liability is tied to the number of distinct targets. It underscores the procedural importance of specificity in applying the hadd of eighty lashes, ensuring justice is neither diluted nor multiplied unjustly. This distinction is crucial in fiqh al-qadhf for determining whether a single legal proceeding suffices or multiple claims must be adjudicated separately.
